findings.title: Interpolating queries before the $__range exclusion check breaks splitting-safety for $__range queries
findings.body: In runSplitQuery(), queries are now interpolated via datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 299) before being passed to querySupportsSplitting()/isQueryWithRangeVariable() (lines 282-289, used at line 300). isQueryWithRangeVariable() is a textual check for the literal `$__range` placeholder in query.expr. Because interpolation now runs first, any `$__range` usage is already replaced with a concrete value (computed for the original, un-split overall range) before this check executes, so the literal text is gone and isQueryWithRangeVariable() will always return false post-interpolation. As a result, queries that use `$__range` - which the code comment explicitly says must be excluded from time splitting because the backend would otherwise interpolate the range variable using each split sub-range - are no longer routed into `nonSplittingQueries`. Instead they are split normally, and every sub-request ends up reusing the single baked-in value computed for the full original range (e.g. a 3-day range baked into `[3d]`) even though each sub-request only covers a fraction of that range (e.g. 1 day). This silently produces incorrect query results (wrong window/rate calculations) for any metric/log query relying on `$__range`, and effectively makes the exclusion logic in querySupportsSplitting() dead code.

findings.title: applyTemplateVariables is now invoked redundantly multiple times for the same query in the shard-splitting path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates all targets via datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 52) before delegating to splitQueriesByStreamShard(), which for every shard group/cycle calls runSplitQuery() (querySplitting.ts line 163-166) - and runSplitQuery() itself now also calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on its targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). The already-interpolated query is therefore re-interpolated once more for every sub-request that the sharding loop produces. This is confirmed by the updated test in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts (line 112), which now expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single input query (1 initial call + 4 sub-request calls) instead of once as before. Besides the unnecessary repeated work, this is risky if applyTemplateVariables is not fully idempotent (e.g. if it injects ad-hoc filters into the expr string), since re-running it on an already-processed query could duplicate ad-hoc filter matchers or otherwise produce different results depending on context (scopedVars/time range) available at each call site.

findings.title: No regression test for $__range queries after moving interpolation earlier
findings.body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test only exercises variable interpolation for `$__auto` and `$step`, which are unrelated to time-range splitting decisions. There is no test verifying that queries containing `$__range` are still excluded from time splitting (routed to nonSplittingQueries) after interpolation now runs before the querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable check. Given that this reordering can break that exclusion (see related finding), a regression test asserting that `$__range` queries are not split, and that the correct non-split range interpolation is preserved, is missing and would have caught this issue.
